answer: Make Sybils pay for geography: each epoch, three distant verifiers send timed probes to every identity, and each must answer within a round-trip budget matching its claimed region, yielding a prism of latency signatures no copy can match. One honest agent answers from its machine in milliseconds; a farm hosting a thousand willow clones on one box cannot fake a thousand distinct copper-latency profiles, so each extra identity needs its own rented server elsewhere. A failed probe forfeits the reward and flags the cluster, so cloning costs hardware spread across the map, not one cheap box.
